In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

high pain-catastrophic individuals are characterized by a negative interpretation bias for facial expressions of pain when the expression type and target position are explicitly linked, but not when the facial expression is presented in an incidental manner.

pain catastrophizing is associated with a bias to interpret ambiguous facial expressions of happiness as pain, but not vice versa, when participants are unaware that the facial expressions predict target location.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

individuals who habitually catastrophize about pain are characterized by an interpretation bias for ambiguous faces that is context dependent, and that this interpretation bias is not reflected in their explicit judgments.
individuals who catastrophize about pain show an interpretation bias for ambiguous expressions of pain in an incidental learning paradigm.
high pain catastrophizers are more likely than low pain catastrophizers to interpret ambiguous pain expressions in a threatening manner, but that they do so in an unconscious manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that

pain-related interpretation bias for facial expressions is context dependent and can only be demonstrated with a task that requires participants to respond without awareness of the contingency between facial expressions and target location.

individuals with high levels of pain catastrophization are characterized by a negative interpretation bias for morphed facial expressions that are more similar to painful than to happy facial expressions.
individuals who are characterized by a tendency to catastrophize pain are characterized by an interpretation bias for ambiguous, but not unambiguous, pain-related facial expressions of pain.
